newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zaire rebel leader in South Africa for talks.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel leader in South Africa for talks.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila arrived in South Africa on Tuesday and was whisked away for what rebel sources said were secret talks on a solution to the Zaire civil war, witnesses said.
His arrival signalled a new step in a tentative peace process begun last week when South Africa hosted secret proximity talks with lower-ranking representatives of the two sides.
The United Nations Information Centre in Johannesburg said the special U.N. envoy on the Great Lakes crisis, Mohamed Sahnoun, had arrived on Tuesday and was likely to have talks with Kabila.
The burly rebel leader arrived at Lanseria airport near Johannesburg at 1215 GMT in a chartered Lear jet from Kigali, Rwanda.

Immediately upon landing, he was escorted by South African intelligence officials to a car parked on the runway, without going through immigration controls. Foreign ministry representatives at the airport declined to comment.
A regional military source earlier told Reuters in Nairobi that Kabila had flown to South Africa for talks with President Nelson Mandela's government on the conflict.
"He left today for South Africa. We do not know how long he will stay. But the visit is part of consultations with the South Africans on the Zaire conflict," the source said.
He added that Kabila would not meet representatives of Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's government during his stay in South Africa.
Mandela's office declined to comment but government sources said if a representative of the Zairean rebels was in the country Mandela would not personally meet with him.
The four-month-old war in Zaire has seen Zaire's ragged government army pitted against rebels of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL).

Kabila left from eastern border city of Goma as rebels and aid workers said Zairean government troops were looting in Kindu and the U.N. World Food Programme said it had reports residents there were panicking.
The rebels, who are trying to oust Mobutu, said they were now only 30 km (18 miles) from the important eastern town of Kindu.

Rebel sources said Kabila was accompanied to South Africa by his chief aide on foreign affairs Bizima Karaha, a medical doctor who last week held talks with South Africa's Deputy President Thabo Mbeki in Cape Town.
Kabila, 56, is from the southern mineral-rich province of Shaba and has opposed Mobutu's rule for more than 30 years.
Rebel spokesman Raphael Nghenda told Reuters his organisation supported talks with government.
"We are the ones who are in a position of force and we are still in favour of negotiations," said Nghenda, adding rebels were still holding off their offensive as a sign of goodwill for negotiations.
The rebels hold a strip stretching at least 1,000 km (600 miles) from the war's starting point on the Rwanda border to Zaire's important southern copper-producing province of Shaba.
